 WASHINGTON — More than 314,000 older Toyota and Lexus vehicles are being recalled due to defective Takata front passenger airbag inflators that could cause serious injury or death, federal safety regulators announced. 
 According to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, long-term exposure to high heat, high humidity, and repeated temperature changes can degrade the chemical propellant inside the inflators.That degradation can cause the metal cartridge to rupture during deployment and propel sharp metal fragments into the vehicle cabin. 
 The recall affects certain 2003-2008 Toyota Corolla, 2005-2006 Tundra, 2005-2007 Sequoia, and 2016-2017 4Runner models, along with 2002-2010 Lexus SC430, 2011 Lexus IS250, and 2017 Lexus GX460 vehicles. No injuries or deaths have been reported in connection with the recall. 
 Toyota plans to begin mailing notification letters to affected owners on Dec.28. Dealerships will replace the passenger airbag inflator or the entire airbag assembly at no cost to vehicle owners.
